# unpatched: the full guide

This file is every page of the guide (https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/) in one text. Generated by `cargo xtask docs`.


---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/index.html

# What is unpatched


unpatched tells you when software you run is affected by a vulnerability, which
version to upgrade to, and whether the bug is being exploited. You write down
what you run, with versions, in one file (`unpatched.yml`). Every day it checks
that list against open vulnerability data and tells you only about what needs
action.

It is for people who run software they did not write and have nobody whose job
it is to watch advisories:

- homelabbers and self-hosters with 5 to 30 things running
- one-person IT teams and small businesses with a firewall, a VPN, a NAS, a
  mail server, a CMS and a few databases
- MSPs that keep one private repository per client

Edge devices with exploited bugs (Fortinet, Ivanti, Citrix, Palo Alto, MOVEit)
and software past its end of life are what get small organisations breached.
Dependabot, Renovate, OSV-Scanner and Trivy cover code and container images, not
a FortiGate or a Nextcloud install. CVE feeds list every CVE for a vendor and
leave the sorting to you. About 40% of CVEs have a CVSS score of 7 or more, so
sorting by CVSS gives mostly noise.

## What you get

- **Told only when it matters.** A finding is one product you run and one
  vulnerability that affects its version. Nothing else is sent.
- **What to do.** Every finding says the version to upgrade to, and for end of
  life software, that you have to move to a supported release.
- **Ranked by exploitation.** The bucket is decided by CISA KEV, the CISA SSVC
  exploitation flag, public exploits, EPSS and whether the item faces the
  internet. See [Findings and rules](findings.md).
- **Evidence for every verdict.** Each finding lists the sources that said so
  and the rule ids behind its bucket. `unpatched explain` shows them. No model
  decides anything.
- **Honest about gaps.** If the data is missing, conflicting or cannot be read,
  the verdict is `unknown`, with the reason. It is never "not affected" without
  evidence.
- **Quiet by default.** A GitHub issue per stack item, a weekly digest in the chat
  channels you choose, and a status issue that says when it last ran, so silence
  never means broken.

## How it works

```text
daily, in the unpatched repository           daily, in your repository
CVE.org, NVD, KEV, EPSS, endoflife.date,     download the database (hash checked)
Exploit-DB, Metasploit ids                   match your stack locally
        |                                    rank findings, compare with last run
        v                                            |
one SQLite database, a release asset  ------->       v
                                             issues, chat messages, report
```

The list of what you run never leaves your repository. See [Privacy](privacy.md).

## Ways to run it

| Way | For |
| --- | --- |
| [GitHub Action](start-github.md) | The main way. A private repository, two files, issues in your inbox. |
| [Command line](start-cli.md) | A laptop, a cron job, a script. `--exit-code` can gate a pipeline. |
| [Docker](start-docker.md) | A homelab server or a NAS that runs a scheduled container. |
| [An AI agent](with-an-agent.md) | "Am I affected by this new Ivanti bug?" answered through an MCP server. |

## What it is not

- **Not a dependency or container scanner.** It does not read your code, lock
  files or images. Use [OSV-Scanner](https://google.github.io/osv-scanner/) or
  [Trivy](https://trivy.dev/) for that. It can check a package you name with a
  `purl`, through OSV, but it does not discover packages.
- **Not a network scanner.** It does not probe hosts or fingerprint versions.
  You say what runs and in which version, and it is only as good as that list.
- **Not a SaaS.** There is no server, no account and no API key. GitHub runs it.
- **Not a guarantee.** It can be wrong, and a quiet report is not proof of
  safety. Read [How accurate is it](accuracy.md).

## Where to go next

- New here: [Start with GitHub](start-github.md).
- Something looks wrong: [Findings and rules](findings.md) and the [FAQ](faq.md).
- Was a CVEWatch user: [Coming from CVEWatch](migrate-from-cvewatch.md).

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/start-github.html

# Start with GitHub


This is the main way to run unpatched. You need a GitHub account and about five
minutes. The Action runs once a day, opens an issue for each finding, and keeps
one status issue up to date. It needs no token of your own and no secret, unless
you also want chat messages.

## 1. Make a private repository

Create a new repository and set it to **Private**. The stack file lists your
software and its versions, which is a map for an attacker. Do not put it in a
public repository. See [the public repository warning](faq.md#can-i-use-a-public-repository).

## 2. Write `unpatched.yml`

Add `unpatched.yml` at the top of the repository. Start from this file (it is
what `unpatched init` writes) and keep only what you run:


```yaml
# unpatched.yml: what you run, and where to tell you.
# Keep this file in a PRIVATE repository: it lists your software and versions.
# Check it with `unpatched check`; `unpatched schema config` prints the format.

# File format version. Only 1 exists.
version: 1

# The software you run. Each entry is either a catalog `product` (find ids with
# `unpatched search <name>`) or a package `purl`.
stack:
  # A firewall that faces the internet. Edge devices are what attackers hit first.
  - product: fortios
    version: 7.2.5
    exposure: internet # internet | internal (default: internal)
    name: Office firewall # your label; tells several instances apart

  - product: nextcloud
    version: 29.0.3
    exposure: internet

  # Quote versions YAML would read as numbers ("15.4" is a number to YAML).
  - product: postgresql
    version: "15.4"

  - product: home-assistant
    version: 2024.10.1

  # A package: unpatched asks OSV about it (needs the network).
  # - purl: pkg:deb/debian/openssl@3.0.11-1~deb12u1?distro=bookworm

# Accept a risk on purpose. `until` is required: nothing is ignored forever, and
# the finding comes back when the date has passed.
# ignore:
#   - cve: CVE-2024-1234
#     product: nextcloud # optional: a product id or a stack `name`; default is all
#     reason: "The app is disabled"
#     until: 2027-01-31

# Where findings go. GitHub issues need no secret and are on by default.
# Secrets are never written here: they come from environment variables
# (repository secrets in GitHub Actions).
notify:
  issues: true
  # telegram:
  #   chat: "123456789" # the bot token is in UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN
  # slack: true # webhook URL in UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK
  # discord: true # webhook URL in UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK
  # ntfy:
  #   topic: my-unpatched-topic # optional token in UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN
  # webhook: true # URL in UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL

# The day of the weekly digest (monday ... sunday), or `daily`. "Fix today"
# findings are sent at once, whatever the day.
digest: monday

# When a finding gets more urgent. The defaults are shown.
# thresholds:
#   epss_week: 0.05 # EPSS at or above this: fix this week
#   cvss_week: 9.0 # CVSS at or above this: fix this week
#   cvss_week_exposed: 7.0 # CVSS at or above this on an internet-facing item: fix this week
#   stale_warn_days: 3 # warn when the database is older than this
#   stale_fail_days: 7 # fail when the database is older than this
```


How to fill it in:

- **`product`**: a catalog id. Run `unpatched search fortigate` (or look in the
  [catalog](catalog.md)) to find it. Aliases work in `search`, but write the id
  in the file.
- **`version`**: the exact version that runs now, from the admin page or
  `--version`. Quote it if YAML would read it as a number: `"15.4"`.
- **`exposure`**: `internet` if it is reachable from the internet (VPN portal,
  web app, mail server), else leave it out. It moves findings up a bucket.
- **`name`**: your own label. Needed to tell two instances of one product apart.
- A package that is not in the catalog (an OS package or a library) can be given
  as a `purl` instead. See the [config reference](config.md).

If a product is not in the catalog, it cannot be matched yet.
[Ask for it](catalog.md#ask-for-a-product).

## 3. Add the workflow

Add `.github/workflows/unpatched.yml`. This is the file `unpatched init --github`
writes:


```yaml
# Checks your stack (unpatched.yml) every day and opens a GitHub issue for each
# finding. Use it in a PRIVATE repository. It needs no token of your own.
name: unpatched

on:
  schedule:
    # Every day at 06:17 UTC. The database is rebuilt at 02:41 UTC.
    - cron: "17 6 * * *"
  # Lets you run it by hand from the Actions tab.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
        # Only for the chat channels you turned on in unpatched.yml.
        # Add each value as a repository secret first (Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions).
        # env:
        #   UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN }}
        #   UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK: ${{ secrets.UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
        #   UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK: ${{ secrets.UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK }}
        #   UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN }}
        #   UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL }}
        with:
          config: unpatched.yml
```


The job needs only `issues: write` (to open and close issues) and
`contents: read` (to read your stack file). It never commits. The database is
built at 02:41 UTC; the default run time is 06:17 UTC, a few hours later. Pick
another time if you like, but a run before 02:41 UTC uses the day-old database,
which is fine.

`amet13/unpatched@v3` runs the newest `v3.x.y` release. To pin one exact
release, use its full tag, such as `@v3.0.0`. See [GitHub Action](action.md).

## 4. Commit, push and run it once

Commit both files and push. A scheduled workflow does not run until its first
schedule, so start it by hand:

1. Open the repository on GitHub, then the **Actions** tab.
2. Choose **unpatched** in the list on the left.
3. Click **Run workflow**, then the green **Run workflow** button.

When the run finishes, open it and read the **summary**: it has
the same table you would get from `unpatched check --format markdown`.

## 5. Read the first result

The first run creates:

- the labels `unpatched`, `unpatched:now`, `unpatched:week`, `unpatched:eol`,
  `unpatched:unknown`, `unpatched:fyi` and `unpatched:status`
- one issue for each stack item that has a finding that is not FYI, labelled with its most urgent bucket
- one **unpatched status** issue (pinned when GitHub allows it) that lists
  everything open, the database date and the time of the last run

GitHub emails you about new issues like any other. How to read an issue and the
rules behind its label: [Findings and rules](findings.md). What closes an issue:
fix it (change the version in `unpatched.yml`), and the next run closes it with a
note. Closing an issue yourself means "I know"; unpatched does not reopen it,
and lists it under "Closed but still affected" in the status issue.

If the first run reports `unknown product`, the id in `unpatched.yml` is not in
the catalog. Read the message: it suggests close matches.

## Private repository, secrets and settings

- **Actions must be on.** In an organization, check that Actions may run
  `amet13/unpatched`, `actions/checkout` and `actions/cache`.
- **No token is needed** for issues. The workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` is used.
- **Secrets** are only for chat channels. Add each one under **Settings,
  Secrets and variables, Actions, New repository secret**, then uncomment the
  matching line in the workflow's `env:` block. Names and details are on
  [Notifications](notifications.md). A secret never goes in `unpatched.yml`.
- **Minutes.** A run is short: it downloads one binary (cached) and one
  database. Private repositories on the free plan have 2,000 Actions minutes a
  month, far more than a daily run uses.
- **Schedules pause in public repositories only.** GitHub turns off scheduled
  workflows after 60 days with no repository activity in a *public* repository.
  In a private one they keep running. See the [FAQ](faq.md#will-the-schedule-stop).

## Change what you run

Edit `unpatched.yml` and push. The next run uses it. To see the result at once,
run the workflow by hand again, or run `unpatched check` on your machine
([Start with the command line](start-cli.md)).

## Test without side effects

Run the Action with `dry-run: true` to print what would happen and send nothing:

```yaml
      - uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
        with:
          dry-run: "true"
```

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `unknown product "..."` | Use an id from `unpatched catalog list`. The message suggests names. |
| `stack[n]: ...` YAML error | Fix the line it shows. `unpatched schema config` prints the format. |
| Exit code 3, "database too old" | The daily database build stopped. See [Data](data.md). |
| `Resource not accessible by integration` | The job lacks `issues: write`. Copy the `permissions:` block above. |
| `check` fails and names an environment variable | A chat channel is on but its secret is not passed in the workflow's `env:` block (exit code 2). |
| A chat message is missing, the rest is fine | The token or URL is wrong, or the service is down. The run exits with code 4 and names the channel. |

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/start-cli.html

# Start with the command line


The command line is for a laptop, a cron job or a script. It does the same
matching as the Action. Without GitHub, it keeps its delivery state in
`.unpatched/state.json` next to your config file.

## Install

| How | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Shell (Linux, macOS) | `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/Amet13/unpatched/releases/latest/download/unpatched-installer.sh \| sh` |
| PowerShell (Windows) | `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://github.com/Amet13/unpatched/releases/latest/download/unpatched-installer.ps1 \| iex"` |
| Homebrew | Download `unpatched.rb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Amet13/unpatched/releases/latest), then `brew install --formula ./unpatched.rb` |
| Cargo | `cargo install unpatched --locked` |
| Archive | Download the `.tar.xz` (Linux, macOS) or `.zip` (Windows) from the releases page, check the `.sha256` file, and put `unpatched` on your `PATH` |

The installers put the binary in `$CARGO_HOME/bin` (usually `~/.cargo/bin`).
There is no Homebrew tap: the formula is a release asset that you install from
a file. Builds exist for Linux (x86_64 and aarch64, static musl), macOS (Intel
and Apple silicon) and Windows (x86_64). Every archive has a GitHub build
attestation: `gh attestation verify <file> --repo Amet13/unpatched`.

Check it works:

```sh
unpatched --version
```

## Write `unpatched.yml`

In a terminal, `unpatched init` asks what you run (it searches the catalog for
each name, asks the version and whether it faces the internet) and writes
`unpatched.yml`. With `--github` it also writes the workflow for the
[GitHub route](start-github.md). When input is not a terminal, it writes the
commented template instead.


```text
$ unpatched init --github
Wrote unpatched.yml
Wrote .github/workflows/unpatched.yml

Next steps:
  1. Edit unpatched.yml: list what you really run, with exact versions.
  2. Run `unpatched check` to see the result.
  3. Keep this repository PRIVATE: unpatched.yml lists your software and versions.
  4. Commit and push both files. The workflow runs every day at 06:17 UTC; start it once from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch).
  5. For Telegram, Slack, Discord, ntfy or a webhook, add the secrets named in unpatched.yml under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions, and uncomment the `env:` lines in the workflow.
```


`init` refuses to overwrite files; add `--force` to do it anyway. Find product
ids without `init`:


```text
$ unpatched search forti
ID            NAME          VENDOR    KIND       VERSIONS
fortimanager  FortiManager  Fortinet  appliance  dotted
fortios       FortiOS       Fortinet  appliance  dotted
fortiproxy    FortiProxy    Fortinet  appliance  dotted
fortiweb      FortiWeb      Fortinet  appliance  dotted

Use the id in unpatched.yml: `product: <id>`.
```


## Run a check

```sh
unpatched check
```

The first run downloads the database (a release asset of this repository, hash
checked) into your cache folder. Later runs reuse it and refresh it when it is
more than 20 hours old. If the refresh fails and an older copy exists, it warns
and uses the older one. See [Data](data.md).

The examples below use a small sample database that is in the repository
(`fixtures/smoke/unpatched-db.sqlite`) and the date 2026-11-24, so you can
compare. Your output uses live data. The stack is the template from above.


```text
$ unpatched check
🔴 FortiOS 7.2.5 (Office firewall)  1 now  →  upgrade to 7.2.7 (fixes 1 of 1)
⚫ Nextcloud 29.0.3  1 eol  →  upgrade to a supported release

🔴 Fix today (1)

  FortiOS 7.2.5 (Office firewall)
  CVE-2024-21762  A out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.2, FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.6, FortiOS 7.0.0 through 7.0.13, For…
    Why   In CISA KEV since 2024-02-09 · ransomware use: known · CISA due date 2024-02-16 · SSVC: exploitation is active · SSVC: automatable · EPSS 84.6% (percentile 100) · CVSS 9.6 · internet-facing
    Do    Upgrade to 7.2.7 or later.
    Rule  UNP-KEV, UNP-SSVC-ACTIVE, UNP-EPSS, UNP-CVSS, UNP-EXPOSED · verdict affected

⚫ End of life (1)

  Nextcloud 29.0.3
  nextcloud 29.0.3 is past end of life: the 29 release cycle no longer gets security fixes
    Why   End of life · internet-facing
    Do    Upgrade to a supported release.
    Rule  UNP-EOL · verdict affected

🟢 1 checked, nothing else affects you
Database: built 2026-11-23 12:00 UTC, 0 days old
Note: stack[2]: the database has no data for product "postgresql" yet. Run `unpatched db update`; if the id may be wrong, `unpatched catalog list` shows the ids.
Note: stack[3]: the database has no data for product "home-assistant" yet. Run `unpatched db update`; if the id may be wrong, `unpatched catalog list` shows the ids.
```


Each finding shows the product and your label, the CVE, why it is in its bucket
(`Why`), what to do (`Do`), and the rule ids. The title of a CVE can be long:
it is the CVE's own description. Read [Findings and rules](findings.md) for the
buckets.

### Formats

`--format` is one of `text` (the default), `json`, `markdown` and `sarif`.
`--output FILE` writes to a file instead of the screen. `json` has a published
schema (`unpatched schema report`), so scripts and agents should read that, not
the text. `sarif` is for code-scanning tools; uploading it to GitHub's Security
tab needs GitHub Advanced Security on private repositories, so unpatched does not
do it for you.

With `--verbose` (or `-v`) the text and Markdown reports include the evidence of
each source.

The same report as `--format json`. Parts are cut out for this page and marked
with `...`: the database sources, the long `title` and `evidence`, and the second
finding.


```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "generated_at": "2026-11-24T00:00:00Z",
  "db": { ... },
  "summary": {
    "now": 1,
    "week": 0,
    "eol": 1,
    "unknown": 0,
    "fyi": 0,
    "ignored": 0,
    "not_affected": 1
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "key": "office-firewall/CVE-2024-21762",
      "item": "Office firewall",
      "product": "fortios",
      "product_name": "FortiOS",
      "version": "7.2.5",
      "exposure": "internet",
      "vuln": "CVE-2024-21762",
      "title": "...",
      "verdict": "affected",
      "bucket": "now",
      "rules": [
        "UNP-KEV",
        "UNP-SSVC-ACTIVE",
        "UNP-EPSS",
        "UNP-CVSS",
        "UNP-EXPOSED"
      ],
      "fixed_in": "7.2.7",
      "latest_in_cycle": null,
      "cvss": {
        "version": "3.1",
        "score": 9.6,
        "vector": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:H/RL:W/RC:C"
      },
      "signals": {
        "kev": {
          "date_added": "2024-02-09",
          "due_date": "2024-02-16",
          "known_ransomware": true,
          "required_action": "Apply mitigations per vendor instructions or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.",
          "vendor_project": "Fortinet",
          "product": "FortiOS"
        },
        "epss": {
          "score": 0.8458899855613708,
          "percentile": 0.9971100091934204,
          "date": "2026-11-23"
        },
        "ssvc_exploitation": "active",
        "ssvc_automatable": true
      },
      "evidence": [ ... ],
      "references": [
        "https://fortiguard.com/psirt/FG-IR-24-015",
        "https://fortiguard.com/psirt/FG-IR-24-015",
        "https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?field_cve=CVE-2024-21762"
      ]
    },
    ...
  ],
  "ignored": [],
  "items": [
    ...
    ...
  ],
  "notes": [
    "stack[2]: the database has no data for product \"postgresql\" yet. Run `unpatched db update`; if the id may be wrong, `unpatched catalog list` shows the ids.",
    "stack[3]: the database has no data for product \"home-assistant\" yet. Run `unpatched db update`; if the id may be wrong, `unpatched catalog list` shows the ids."
  ]
}
```


### Packages and the network

A `purl` item in `unpatched.yml` is looked up live in OSV (see
[Privacy](privacy.md)). `--offline` skips that and the database download. Catalog
products still work with `--offline` when a database is on disk. Use
`--db FILE` (or `$UNPATCHED_DB`) to choose the database file.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | OK |
| 1 | `check --exit-code` found something to fix today |
| 2 | Usage or configuration error (bad YAML, unknown product, missing secret) |
| 3 | Data error (no database, database too old, a download failed) |
| 4 | Delivery error (a chat channel or GitHub issue failed) |

`--exit-code` makes `check` return 1 when there is a "fix today" finding, so a
script or pipeline can stop:

```sh
unpatched check --exit-code --quiet || echo "something to fix today"
```

A database older than `stale_fail_days` (7 by default) stops the run with
exit code 3. `--allow-stale` overrides that. At `stale_warn_days` (3) you get a
finding that says the data is old.

## Send messages from the command line

`--notify` sends the findings to the channels in `unpatched.yml`. Outside GitHub
Actions it uses the local state file to avoid repeats. `--dry-run` prints what
would be sent and sends nothing. Secrets come from environment variables. See
[Notifications](notifications.md).

```sh
export UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN=...   # only if your ntfy topic needs one
unpatched check --notify
```

A cron entry that runs it every morning:

```text
17 6 * * *  cd /home/me/stack && unpatched check --notify --quiet
```

`--github` makes the command keep issues and state in a GitHub repository (it
needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`). It is on by itself inside GitHub
Actions.

## Look closer

Show the evidence for a CVE, and what a rule means:


```text
$ unpatched explain CVE-2024-21762
CVE-2024-21762
  A out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.2, FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.6, FortiOS 7.0.0 through 7.0.13, FortiOS 6.4.0 through 6.4.14, FortiOS 6.2.0 through 6.2.15, FortiOS 6.0 all versions, FortiProxy 7.4.0 through 7.4.2, FortiProxy 7.2.0 through 7.2.8, FortiProxy 7.0.0 through 7.0.14, FortiProxy 2.0.0 through 2.0.13, FortiProxy 01.02 all versions, FortiProxy 1.2 all versions, FortiProxy 01.01 all versions, FortiProxy 1.1 all versions, FortiProxy 01.00 all versions allows attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via specifically crafted requests
  status: published · published 2024-02-09 · modified 2026-10-22
  CVSS 3.1: 9.6 CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:H/RL:W/RC:C

Exploitation signals
  CISA KEV: added 2024-02-09, due 2024-02-16, ransomware use: known
  EPSS: 84.6% (percentile 100) on 2026-11-23
  SSVC exploitation: Active, automatable: yes
...
```



```text
$ unpatched explain UNP-KEV
UNP-KEV: Known to be exploited

CISA lists this vulnerability in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, so attackers are using it now. Fix it today.

This rule puts an affected finding in: Fix today (now).
```


With a stack file, `explain CVE-...` also shows what the CVE means for your
items, and `explain <item>/<CVE>` explains one finding by its key (the key is in
the JSON report and in the hidden marker of each issue).

Show a catalog entry, the names it matches in each source:


```text
$ unpatched catalog show fortios
# catalog/fortios.yml
id: fortios
name: FortiOS
vendor: Fortinet
kind: appliance
versioning: dotted
match:
  cpe:
  - fortinet:fortios
  cna:
  - vendor: Fortinet
    product: FortiOS
  - vendor: Fortinet
    product: Fortinet FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiSwitchManager
  - vendor: Fortinet
    product: FortiOS-6K7K
  kev:
  - vendorProject: Fortinet
    product: FortiOS
  - vendorProject: Fortinet
    product: FortiOS and FortiProxy
  - vendorProject: Fortinet
    product: FortiOS and FortiProxy SSL-VPN
  - vendorProject: Fortinet
    product: FortiOS and FortiADC
eol: fortios
aliases:
- fortigate
- fortinet firewall
homepage: https://www.fortinet.com/products/fortigate/fortios
checked: 2026-11-23
```


Check how old the database is:


```text
$ unpatched db info
File:             fixtures/smoke/unpatched-db.sqlite
Schema version:   1
Built:            2026-11-23 12:00 UTC (0 days old)
Products:         7 (6 found in the data)
Vulnerabilities:  7
Sources:
  CISA KEV        ok  7 records   2026-11-23 12:00 UTC
  EPSS            ok  8 records   2026-11-23 12:00 UTC
  NVD             ok  2 records   2026-11-23 12:00 UTC  1 feeds, 7 records scanned
  CVE.org         ok  14 records  2026-11-23 12:00 UTC
  endoflife.date  ok  1 records   2026-11-23 12:00 UTC
  Exploit-DB      ok  9 records   2026-11-23 12:00 UTC
  Metasploit      ok  9 records   2026-11-23 12:00 UTC
```


`unpatched db update` downloads the latest database now. `unpatched db build`
builds one from the sources yourself (slow; the repository does it daily), for
people who do not want to trust the published one. The
[command reference](cli.md) lists every command and option.

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/start-docker.html

# Start with Docker


The image `ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched` holds the `unpatched` binary and nothing
else (a static build on a distroless base, running as a non-root user). It is
for a homelab server or a NAS that can run a scheduled container, when you do not
want GitHub Actions.

Tags: a full version (`3.0.0`), `3.0`, `3` and `latest`. Pin a version if you want
upgrades to be your decision. The image is built for `linux/amd64` and
`linux/arm64`.

## Run it

Make a folder with your `unpatched.yml` ([how to write it](start-github.md)) and
run the image with that folder mounted at `/work`:

```sh
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e UNPATCHED_CACHE_DIR=/work/.cache \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched
```

With no arguments the image runs `unpatched check --notify`. Why each option:

- `-v "$PWD:/work"`: the container's working directory is `/work`, where it
  looks for `unpatched.yml` and where it saves `.unpatched/state.json` (what was
  already sent, so you get no repeats).
- `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`: files it writes in the folder belong to you.
- `UNPATCHED_CACHE_DIR=/work/.cache`: the database (a few tens of MB) is kept
  there between runs instead of being downloaded each time.

Add `.cache/` and `.unpatched/` to your `.gitignore` if the folder is a
repository. Keep it private: `unpatched.yml` lists your software.

Any other command works by adding it after the image name:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched check --format markdown
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched explain CVE-2024-21762
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched search nextcloud
```

## Secrets

Chat channels need a secret in an environment variable (names are on
[Notifications](notifications.md)). Pass it through from your shell or an env
file, so it never appears in the command line:

```sh
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e UNPATCHED_CACHE_DIR=/work/.cache \
  -e UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched
```

or `--env-file unpatched.env` with the file outside any repository.

GitHub issues are not used outside GitHub Actions, unless you set `GITHUB_TOKEN`
and `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and add `--github`. With plain Docker, the chat channels
and the report are what you have.

## On a schedule

Cron on the host:

```text
17 6 * * *  cd /srv/unpatched && docker run --rm --user 1000:1000 -e UNPATCHED_CACHE_DIR=/work/.cache --env-file /srv/unpatched.env -v /srv/unpatched:/work ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched --quiet check --notify
```

(Use your own user id.) A Compose service that you start with
`docker compose run --rm unpatched`:

```yaml
services:
  unpatched:
    image: ghcr.io/amet13/unpatched:0
    user: "1000:1000"
    environment:
      UNPATCHED_CACHE_DIR: /work/.cache
      UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN: ${UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN}
    volumes:
      - ./:/work
```

The exit code tells your scheduler how it went: see
[Exit codes](start-cli.md#exit-codes). A run that finds something to fix today
only exits with 1 when you add `--exit-code`.

## Use it from an MCP client

The MCP server runs in the image too, for agents that start servers with Docker.
See [With an agent](with-an-agent.md#docker).

## Build it yourself

```sh
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t unpatched .
```

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/config.html

# Config reference


`unpatched.yml` says what you run and where to tell you. It is read by every
command (`--config FILE` chooses another path). Keep it in a private repository.

The file is YAML. Unknown keys are an error, so a typo such as `exposur:` is
reported with its line instead of being ignored. Only `version` and `stack` are
required. `unpatched schema config` prints the JSON Schema, which most editors
can use for completion; it is also in `schema/unpatched.schema.json`.

## A complete example

```yaml
version: 1

stack:
  - product: fortios
    version: 7.2.5
    exposure: internet
    name: Office firewall
  - product: fortios
    version: 7.0.13
    name: Lab firewall
  - product: nextcloud
    version: 29.0.3
    exposure: internet
  - product: postgresql
    version: "15.4"
  - purl: pkg:deb/debian/openssl@3.0.11-1~deb12u1?distro=bookworm

ignore:
  - cve: CVE-2024-1234
    product: nextcloud
    reason: The app is disabled
    until: 2027-01-31

notify:
  issues: true
  telegram:
    chat: "123456789"
  ntfy:
    topic: my-unpatched-topic

digest: monday

thresholds:
  epss_week: 0.1
  cvss_week: 8.0
```

## Keys


### Top level

| Key | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | integer | yes | none | File format version. Only `1` exists. |
| `stack` | list of `stack[]` | yes | none | The software you run, one entry per instance. |
| `ignore` | list of `ignore[]` | no | none | Risks you accept on purpose, each with a reason and an end date. |
| `notify` | object (see `notify`) | no | none | Channels. Secrets (tokens, webhook URLs) never go here: they come from environment variables named in the docs (`UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, …). |
| `digest` | string | no | `monday` | Day of the weekly digest (`monday` … `sunday`), or `daily`. |
| `thresholds` | object (see `thresholds`) | no | none | When a finding gets more urgent. |

### `stack[]`

One thing you run. Give either `product` (a catalog id) or `purl` (a package).

| Key | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | string | no | none | Catalog product id (`unpatched catalog list`). |
| `purl` | string | no | none | Package URL with version, e.g. `pkg:deb/debian/openssl@3.0.11-1~deb12u1?distro=bookworm`. |
| `version` | string | no | none | Required with `product`; taken from the purl otherwise. |
| `exposure` | `internet` or `internal` | no | `internal` | Whether the item is reachable from the internet. It can move a finding up a bucket. |
| `name` | string | no | none | Your label, e.g. "Office firewall". Tells instances apart. |

### `ignore[]`

Accept a risk on purpose. `until` is required: nothing is ignored forever.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cve` | string | yes | none | The CVE (or advisory) id to ignore. |
| `product` | string | no | none | Only for this product id (or stack item `name`); all items when empty. |
| `reason` | string | yes | none | Why you accept the risk. Shown in the report. |
| `until` | date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) | yes | none | The last day the entry applies. After it the finding comes back. |

### `notify`

Channels. Secrets (tokens, webhook URLs) never go here: they come from environment variables named in the docs (`UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, …).

| Key | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `issues` | true or false | no | `true` | GitHub Issues in the repository the Action runs in. |
| `telegram` | object (see `notify.telegram`) | no | none | Send messages to a Telegram chat. |
| `slack` | true or false | no | `false` | Slack incoming webhook (URL in `UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK`). |
| `discord` | true or false | no | `false` | Discord webhook (URL in `UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`). |
| `ntfy` | object (see `notify.ntfy`) | no | none | Send messages to an ntfy topic. |
| `webhook` | true or false | no | `false` | Generic JSON webhook (URL in `UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL`). |

### `notify.telegram`

| Key | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat` | string | yes | none | Chat id. The bot token comes from `UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`. |

### `notify.ntfy`

| Key | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | string | yes | none | The ntfy topic to publish to. |
| `server` | string | no | `https://ntfy.sh` | The ntfy server. |

### `thresholds`

| Key | Type | Required | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `epss_week` | number | no | `0.05` | EPSS score at or above which an affected finding is at least `week`. |
| `cvss_week` | number | no | `9.0` | CVSS base score at or above which an affected finding is at least `week`. |
| `stale_warn_days` | integer | no | `3` | Days after which the database counts as stale (warning). |
| `stale_fail_days` | integer | no | `7` | Days after which a run fails because the data is too old. |
| `cvss_week_exposed` | number | no | `7.0` | CVSS base score at or above which an affected, internet-facing finding is at least `week`. |

Unknown keys are an error: `additionalProperties` is `false` everywhere, so a typo is caught instead of ignored. The same schema is in `schema/unpatched.schema.json` and is printed by `unpatched schema config`.


## The stack

Each entry is one thing you run. Give either `product` or `purl`, never both.

**A catalog product** has `product` (an id from `unpatched catalog list`) and
`version`. This is the better choice when the product is in the
[catalog](catalog.md): matching is aware of the product's version scheme, end of
life dates come from endoflife.date, and findings can name the fixed version.

**A package** has `purl`, a [package URL](https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec)
with the version after `@`: `pkg:deb/debian/openssl@3.0.11-1~deb12u1?distro=bookworm`,
`pkg:apk/alpine/curl@8.5.0-r0?distro=alpine-3.19`, `pkg:pypi/django@3.2.0`,
`pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.15`. Packages are looked up live in OSV, so they need the
network and are skipped with `--offline`. See [Privacy](privacy.md) for what is
sent.

**Several instances** of one product are several entries. Give each a `name`,
so findings say which one. The name also becomes the start of the finding's key
(`office-firewall/CVE-2024-21762`).

**Versions** are compared by the product's own scheme (dotted numbers, semver,
calendar versions, Debian, RPM, APK, PEP 440). If a version cannot be read in
that scheme, the verdict is `unknown` with the reason, never a guess. Quote
versions that YAML could read as numbers (`"15.4"`).

**`exposure`** is `internet` (reachable from the internet: VPN portals, web
apps, mail servers) or `internal`, the default. It changes the bucket: an
affected, internet-facing item is at least "fix this week", and with a public
exploit it is "fix today". Mark only what really is reachable.

## Ignore entries

An ignore entry accepts a risk on purpose, like a VEX statement "not affected
because...":

```yaml
ignore:
  - cve: CVE-2024-1234
    product: nextcloud          # optional: a product id or a stack `name`
    reason: The app is disabled
    until: 2027-01-31
```

- `cve`, `reason` and `until` are required. There is no "ignore forever":
  `until` is the last day the entry applies.
- Without `product`, the entry covers every stack item that the CVE affects.
  With it, only the item whose product id or `name` matches.
- An ignored finding leaves the main report and is listed under "ignored", with
  the reason and date (rule `UNP-IGNORED`). Its GitHub issue is closed with a
  note.
- When the date has passed, the finding is back in its bucket with the rule
  `UNP-IGNORE-EXPIRED`, and the issue is reopened.

## Thresholds

Every number has a default; set only what you want to change.

```yaml
thresholds:
  epss_week: 0.05
  cvss_week: 9.0
  cvss_week_exposed: 7.0
  stale_warn_days: 3
  stale_fail_days: 7
```

- `epss_week`: an affected finding with an EPSS score at or above this is at
  least "this week" (rule `UNP-EPSS`). EPSS is the estimated probability of
  exploitation in the next 30 days, from 0 to 1.
- `cvss_week`: the same for the CVSS base score (rule `UNP-CVSS`).
- `cvss_week_exposed`: the CVSS base score at or above which an internet-facing item's finding is `week` (rule `UNP-EXPOSED`, default 7.0).
- `stale_warn_days`: when the database is older than this, the report has a
  finding that says so (rule `UNP-STALE-DATA`).
- `stale_fail_days`: when it is older than this, the run stops with exit code 3.
  `check --allow-stale` overrides it.

The "fix today" conditions (KEV, SSVC active, public exploit on an internet-facing
item) have no threshold. See [Findings and rules](findings.md).

## Notifications

```yaml
notify:
  issues: true          # GitHub issues; the default
  telegram:
    chat: "123456789"   # token in UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN
  slack: true           # webhook URL in UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK
  discord: true         # webhook URL in UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK
  ntfy:
    topic: my-topic     # optional: server (default https://ntfy.sh); token in UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN
  webhook: true         # URL in UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL, optional signing secret in UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_SECRET

digest: monday          # monday ... sunday, or daily
```

Secrets are never read from this file. If a channel is turned on and its
variable is missing, the run stops with exit code 2 and names the variable. Each
channel, with an example message, is on [Notifications](notifications.md).

`digest` is the day of the weekly digest sent to chat channels. It does not delay
"fix today" findings, which are sent once as soon as they appear.

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/findings.html

# Findings and rules


A **finding** is one thing you run and one vulnerability that matters for it. It
has a **verdict** (is your version affected?), a **bucket** (how soon to act)
and **rules** (why it is in that bucket). The end of life of a release and a few
problems with the data are findings too.

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `affected` | Your version is inside an affected range that at least one source gives. |
| `fixed` | It was affected and your version is now at or past the fix. Used to close issues. |
| `not-affected` | At least one source has data and every source with data says your version is outside its ranges. Not reported. |
| `unknown` | The data cannot say: no source has version data yet (new CVEs often wait for NVD analysis), your version cannot be read in the product's scheme, or the product is not found in the data. |

Every source is judged on its own, then the verdicts are combined. One source
saying `affected` is enough. `not-affected` needs evidence: having no data is
never "not affected". When sources disagree the finding is reported and the rule
`UNP-CONFLICT` is added, so you can read the evidence and decide. The reasoning is
in the decision record ADR-0006.

An `unknown` is not shown for every vulnerability that lacks data: that would
bury the report. It is shown only when the signals would have made it "fix today"
or "this week" if it were confirmed (for example a CVE in KEV for your product
with no version range yet). The reason is given in the finding.

## Buckets

The bucket is decided by evidence of exploitation first, not by severity.

| Bucket | Label | When (for an `affected` finding) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `now` | Fix today | In CISA KEV, or CISA SSVC says exploitation is active, or a public exploit exists (Exploit-DB or Metasploit) and the item is `exposure: internet`. |
| `week` | Fix this week | EPSS at or above `epss_week` (default 0.05), or CVSS at or above `cvss_week` (default 9.0), or the item is `exposure: internet` and CVSS is at or above `cvss_week_exposed` (default 7.0). Exposure alone is not enough, and an unknown CVSS score does not count. |
| `fyi` | FYI | Any other affected finding. No issue is opened for it; it is listed in the status issue and the digest. |
| `eol` | End of life | The release cycle of the item is past its end of life (endoflife.date). One finding per item, not one per CVE. |
| `unknown` | Unknown | An `unknown` verdict that would have been `now` or `week` if confirmed, or a data problem (product not found, stale database). |

The first matching bucket wins, from the top. A `now` finding lists the `week`
rules too, so you see every reason. Thresholds can be changed in
[the config](config.md#thresholds); the other conditions cannot. The reasoning
(why not CVSS) is in ADR-0008.

For an affected finding, `fixed_in` is the lowest version that fixes it, taken
from the upper bound of the affected range. `latest_in_cycle` is the newest
release in your release cycle from endoflife.date, shown when it is newer.

## Read a GitHub issue

There is one issue per stack item, not one per CVE. The title is the most urgent
bucket's emoji, the product and version, how many findings are in that bucket and
the one upgrade that helps most, like `🔴 FortiOS 7.2.5 (Office firewall): 14 to fix
today — upgrade to 7.2.12`. Labels: `unpatched` and the label of the most urgent
bucket (`unpatched:now`, `unpatched:week`, `unpatched:eol` or `unpatched:unknown`).
This is the body the renderer writes for an item with a "fix today" finding (the
renderer's own test fixture, so the CVE text and numbers differ from the sample
database):


```markdown
🔴 FortiOS 7.2.5 (Office firewall)  1 now  →  upgrade to 7.2.7 (fixes 1 of 1)

This item is marked as internet-facing.

### 🔴 Fix today (1)

- **CVE-2024-21762** Out-of-bounds write in sslvpnd allows remote code execution — In CISA KEV since 2024-02-09 · ransomware use: known · CISA due date 2024-02-16 · SSVC: exploitation is active · SSVC: automatable · EPSS 94.1% (percentile 100) · public exploit: fortios_sslvpnd · CVSS 9.8 · internet-facing — Upgrade to 7.2.7 or later (7.2.11 is current in this branch).

---

unpatched keeps this issue up to date and closes it once the item has nothing left to fix (when the version in unpatched.yml is fixed).

<!-- unpatched:item=office-firewall -->
```


- The first line is the recommendation for the item: counts per bucket and the
  smallest version that fixes the most findings (`fixes 48 of 50`).
- Then one section per bucket lists its findings: id, a one-sentence title, why
  it is in that bucket, and what to do. A long list stops after about 60 entries
  with "...and N more (run `unpatched check` for all)".
- The hidden comment at the end (`<!-- unpatched:item=... -->`) is how unpatched
  finds the issue again. Do not remove it.

When an item has no `now`, `week`, `eol` or `unknown` finding left (you upgraded,
the advisories were withdrawn, or ignore entries cover them), unpatched comments on
the issue and closes it. If findings come back, an issue that unpatched closed is
reopened. An issue that *you* closed
is left closed, and is listed under "Closed but still affected" in the status
issue.

## The status issue

One issue called **unpatched status** (label `unpatched:status`, pinned when
GitHub allows it) is rewritten on every run. It has the count per bucket, the
open findings with links to their issues, FYI findings, issues you closed that
are still affected, notes, the date of the database and the time of the last run.
It also holds a hidden block with what was already sent to chat channels, so
messages are not repeated. Do not delete it: the next run would make a new one
and may repeat messages once. More in [Notifications](notifications.md#how-state-works).

## Read the JSON report

`unpatched check --format json` prints the report. It has a published schema:
`unpatched schema report` (also `schema/report.schema.json`). Scripts and agents
should read this, not the text output. One, with parts cut out for this page and
marked with `...` (the database sources, the long `title` and `evidence`, and the
second finding):


```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "generated_at": "2026-11-24T00:00:00Z",
  "db": { ... },
  "summary": {
    "now": 1,
    "week": 0,
    "eol": 1,
    "unknown": 0,
    "fyi": 0,
    "ignored": 0,
    "not_affected": 1
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "key": "office-firewall/CVE-2024-21762",
      "item": "Office firewall",
      "product": "fortios",
      "product_name": "FortiOS",
      "version": "7.2.5",
      "exposure": "internet",
      "vuln": "CVE-2024-21762",
      "title": "...",
      "verdict": "affected",
      "bucket": "now",
      "rules": [
        "UNP-KEV",
        "UNP-SSVC-ACTIVE",
        "UNP-EPSS",
        "UNP-CVSS",
        "UNP-EXPOSED"
      ],
      "fixed_in": "7.2.7",
      "latest_in_cycle": null,
      "cvss": {
        "version": "3.1",
        "score": 9.6,
        "vector": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:H/RL:W/RC:C"
      },
      "signals": {
        "kev": {
          "date_added": "2024-02-09",
          "due_date": "2024-02-16",
          "known_ransomware": true,
          "required_action": "Apply mitigations per vendor instructions or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.",
          "vendor_project": "Fortinet",
          "product": "FortiOS"
        },
        "epss": {
          "score": 0.8458899855613708,
          "percentile": 0.9971100091934204,
          "date": "2026-11-23"
        },
        "ssvc_exploitation": "active",
        "ssvc_automatable": true
      },
      "evidence": [ ... ],
      "references": [
        "https://fortiguard.com/psirt/FG-IR-24-015",
        "https://fortiguard.com/psirt/FG-IR-24-015",
        "https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?field_cve=CVE-2024-21762"
      ]
    },
    ...
  ],
  "ignored": [],
  "items": [
    ...
    ...
  ],
  "notes": [
    "stack[2]: the database has no data for product \"postgresql\" yet. Run `unpatched db update`; if the id may be wrong, `unpatched catalog list` shows the ids.",
    "stack[3]: the database has no data for product \"home-assistant\" yet. Run `unpatched db update`; if the id may be wrong, `unpatched catalog list` shows the ids."
  ]
}
```


`summary` counts the findings per bucket, plus `ignored` and `not_affected`. Each
finding has its `key` (stable across runs), `verdict`, `bucket`, `rules`,
`fixed_in`, `latest_in_cycle`, `cvss`, `signals` (KEV, EPSS, SSVC, exploits),
`evidence` per source and `references`. `notes` lists problems with the run
itself: an unknown product id, a stale database, a version that cannot be
compared.

## Explain a finding

```sh
unpatched explain UNP-KEV                         # what a rule means
unpatched explain CVE-2024-21762                  # the record: ranges per source, signals
unpatched explain office-firewall/CVE-2024-21762  # one finding of your stack, with its evidence
```

The finding key is `<item>/<vulnerability>`, where the item is your `name`
(lowercased, spaces become `-`) or the product id. Examples are on
[Start with the command line](start-cli.md#look-closer).

## Every rule

Rule ids are part of the public interface: they do not change meaning, and
renaming one would be a breaking change.


| Rule | Title | What it means | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `UNP-KEV` | Known to be exploited | CISA lists this vulnerability in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, so attackers are using it now. Fix it today. | This rule puts an affected finding in: Fix today (now). |
| `UNP-SSVC-ACTIVE` | Exploitation is active | CISA's SSVC assessment says exploitation of this vulnerability is active. Treat it like a known exploited vulnerability and fix it today. | This rule puts an affected finding in: Fix today (now). |
| `UNP-EXPLOIT-EXPOSED` | Public exploit and reachable from the internet | A public exploit exists (Exploit-DB or Metasploit) and this item is marked as internet-facing. Anyone can try it against you, so fix it today. | This rule puts an affected finding in: Fix today (now). |
| `UNP-EPSS` | Likely to be exploited soon | The EPSS score is at or above your threshold (default 0.05), which means exploitation in the next 30 days is more likely than for most vulnerabilities. Fix it this week. | This rule puts an affected finding in: This week (week), unless a Fix today rule applies. |
| `UNP-CVSS` | Critical severity | The CVSS base score is at or above your threshold (default 9.0). Severity alone does not mean it is being exploited, but it is serious enough to fix this week. | This rule puts an affected finding in: This week (week), unless a Fix today rule applies. |
| `UNP-EXPOSED` | Affected, reachable from the internet and severe | This version is affected, the item is marked as internet-facing and the CVSS base score is at or above your exposed threshold (default 7.0). Attackers can reach it, so fix it this week. | This rule puts an affected, internet-facing finding with CVSS at or above cvss_week_exposed in: This week (week), unless a Fix today rule applies. |
| `UNP-AFFECTED` | Affected, no sign of exploitation | This version is affected, but nothing says it is exploited, it is not both internet-facing and severe, and the scores are below your thresholds. Fix it with your normal updates. | This rule puts an affected finding in: FYI (fyi). |
| `UNP-EOL` | End of life | This release cycle no longer gets security fixes (endoflife.date). New vulnerabilities will not be patched, so plan an upgrade to a supported cycle. | This rule makes the finding: End of life (eol), one per stack item. |
| `UNP-UNKNOWN-NO-RANGES` | No usable version data yet | No source says which versions are affected (new CVEs often wait for NVD analysis). It could matter, so check the advisory yourself. The finding goes away when data arrives. | This rule makes the verdict unknown; shown when the signals would make it Fix today or This week. |
| `UNP-UNKNOWN-VERSION` | Version cannot be compared | Either your configured version or a version in the data does not parse under this product's version scheme. unpatched does not guess, so check the version in unpatched.yml. | This rule makes the verdict unknown; shown when the signals would make it Fix today or This week. |
| `UNP-CONFLICT` | Sources disagree | One source says this version is affected and another says it is not. A source that only says "all versions" does not outweigh one with exact ranges, so the verdict is unknown. Read the evidence to see which source to trust. | This rule is added when sources disagree; it makes the verdict unknown when the only "affected" comes from a source that says all versions. |
| `UNP-UNVERIFIED-PRODUCT` | Product not found in the data | The catalog's names for this product match no record in the database, so an empty result would not mean you are safe. Check the catalog entry or report it. | This rule makes a finding in: Unknown, so an empty result is never read as safe. |
| `UNP-IGNORED` | Ignored on purpose | An ignore entry in unpatched.yml accepts this risk until its date. The finding is listed separately and comes back when the entry expires. | This rule moves the finding to the ignored list. |
| `UNP-IGNORE-EXPIRED` | Ignore entry has expired | An ignore entry matched this finding but its date has passed, so the finding is back. Fix the issue or write a new entry with a new date. | This rule is added when an ignore entry ran out. |
| `UNP-STALE-DATA` | Data is out of date | The vulnerability database is older than your warning threshold (default 3 days). Results may miss new vulnerabilities, so check that the daily database build is running. | This rule makes a finding in: Unknown about the database itself. |

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/notifications.html

# Notifications


unpatched tells you in three kinds of message:

| Message | When |
| --- | --- |
| Alert | A finding that is "fix today" is new, or has just become "fix today". Sent once. |
| Digest | On your digest day (`digest:` in `unpatched.yml`, default `monday`), even when nothing needs action: the footer says how many items were checked and how old the database is, so silence never means broken. Also sent if the last one is 7 or more days old. |
| Resolved | A finding that you were told about is gone. |

GitHub issues work differently: one issue per stack item, opened and closed as the
item's findings change. See [Findings and rules](findings.md#read-a-github-issue).

Chat channels are opt-in. Add them in `unpatched.yml` and give each its secret in
an environment variable. In GitHub Actions, add a repository secret and pass it
in the workflow's `env:` block (the workflow template has the lines, commented
out). Elsewhere, export the variable. A secret is never read from
`unpatched.yml`, and never printed in logs or error messages.

If a channel is on and its variable is missing, `check --notify` stops with exit
code 2 and names every missing variable at once. If a channel fails to deliver
(wrong token, service down), the others are still delivered and the run exits
with code 4.

## Channels

| Channel | In `unpatched.yml` | Environment variable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub issues | `issues: true` (default) | none; the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `issues: write` |
| Telegram | `telegram: { chat: "123456789" }` | `UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` (the bot token) |
| Slack | `slack: true` | `UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK` (an incoming webhook URL) |
| Discord | `discord: true` | `UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK` (a webhook URL) |
| ntfy | `ntfy: { topic: "my-topic" }` | `UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN`, optional (for a protected topic) |
| Webhook | `webhook: true` | `UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL`; `UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, optional |

### GitHub issues

On by default inside GitHub Actions (and with `check --github`). Needs the job
permission `issues: write` and nothing else. Outside GitHub it is skipped.
FYI findings do not get an issue; the others do, with a label for the bucket. Set
`issues: false` to turn it off, for example if you only want chat messages.

### Telegram

Create a bot with [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) and copy its token into
`UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`. Send the bot a message, then find your chat id (for
example with `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates`) and put it in
`chat`. Keep the id quoted. Messages are sent with MarkdownV2 and are cut to fit
Telegram's length limit ("...and 3 more").

### Slack

Create an [incoming webhook](https://api.slack.com/messaging/webhooks) for a
channel and store its URL in `UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK`.

### Discord

In the channel settings, Integrations, Webhooks, make a webhook and store its URL
in `UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`. Messages do not mention anyone.

### ntfy

Set `topic`. The default server is `https://ntfy.sh`; use `server` for your own.
If the topic needs authentication, put the access token in `UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN`.
Anyone who knows a public topic name can read it, so choose a long random name.

```yaml
notify:
  ntfy:
    topic: unpatched-8f3k29dkq1
    server: https://ntfy.example.org
```

### Webhook

A JSON `POST` to the URL in `UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL`, for your own tooling:

```json
{
  "event": "alert",
  "generated_at": "2026-11-24T06:17:00Z",
  "summary": { "now": 1, "week": 0, "eol": 1, "unknown": 0, "fyi": 0, "ignored": 0, "not_affected": 1 },
  "findings": [ { "key": "office-firewall/CVE-2024-21762", "bucket": "now" } ],
  "report_url": "https://github.com/me/stack/actions/runs/123"
}
```

`event` is `alert`, `digest` or `resolved`; each finding is shaped like a finding
of [the JSON report](findings.md#read-the-json-report) (the example above is cut
down). A `resolved` message has a `resolved` list of keys. `report_url` is set
inside GitHub Actions. If you set `UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, the request carries
`X-Unpatched-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, the HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body bytes
with that secret. Check it before you trust the request.

## Example messages

An alert (plain text; Slack, Discord and Telegram get the same lines with their
own bold and escaping). This is the renderer's own test fixture:


```text
unpatched · 1 to fix today

🔴 Fix today  FortiOS 7.2.5 (Office firewall): CVE-2024-21762, exploited, upgrade to 7.2.7+

🟢 1,412 checked, nothing else affects you
Database: built 2026-11-22 02:41 UTC, 1 day old
https://example.com/r
```


A digest, with one line per item and bucket, `(new)` for findings since the last
digest, and a footer that says it is still running:


```text
unpatched · week 48

🔴  FortiOS 7.2.5 (Office firewall): 1 now → upgrade to 7.2.7 (fixes 1 of 1)
🟡  Nextcloud 29.0.3: 2 week → upgrade to 29.0.8 (fixes 2 of 2)
⚫  PostgreSQL 13.12: 1 eol → upgrade to a supported release
❔  Home Assistant 2024.10.1: 1 unknown
⚪  Redis 7.2.1: 1 fyi → upgrade to 7.2.4 (fixes 1 of 1)

🟢 1,412 checked, nothing else affects you
Database: built 2026-11-22 02:41 UTC, 1 day old
```


## How state works

unpatched must not repeat itself, and must close what is fixed. It needs to
remember what it already told you, and it does this without committing anything
to your repository.

**In GitHub Actions** the state lives in GitHub itself:

- Each finding issue has a hidden marker, `<!-- unpatched:finding=<key> -->`. A
  run finds its issues by that marker, and creates, updates, closes or reopens
  them to match the report.
- The pinned **unpatched status** issue holds, in a hidden JSON block, which
  findings were seen, in which bucket, and which channels were told. That is how
  an alert is sent once, and how a chat channel you add later still gets the
  open "fix today" findings once.
- The Action never commits and needs only `issues: write`.

If you delete the status issue, the next run makes a new one and may repeat
messages once. A finding that becomes "fix today" is announced even if it was
reported in a lower bucket before.

**On the command line or in Docker** the same state is kept in
`.unpatched/state.json`, next to your config file. Keep that file between runs.
A run with `--dry-run` writes nothing.

The state is as durable as the issues or the file. Both stores hold the same
information. Treat both as private, like `unpatched.yml`: they name your items
and versions.

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/catalog.html

# Catalog


Sources name the same product in different ways: NVD writes CPE names
(`fortinet:fortios`), CVE records use the vendor's own words (`Fortinet` /
`FortiOS`), CISA KEV has its own pair, and endoflife.date has a slug. The catalog
is one small YAML file per product (`catalog/<id>.yml`) that ties these names
together, and says how the product's versions are compared.

You use the catalog id in `unpatched.yml`:

```yaml
stack:
  - product: fortios
    version: 7.2.5
```

Find an id with `unpatched search <words>` (it matches the id, name, vendor and
aliases such as `fortigate`) or `unpatched catalog list`. `unpatched catalog show <id>`
prints the whole entry.

71 products.


Columns:

- **Versions** is the scheme used to compare versions of this product: `dotted`
  (numbers separated by dots), `semver`, `calver`, `debian`, `rpm`, `apk`,
  `pep440` or a named custom scheme.
- **End of life** says whether the product has an endoflife.date slug. If it does,
  `unpatched` reports a release cycle that is past its end of life. If it does not
  (endoflife.date has no page for it), end of life is not checked for that product.
- **Checked** is the date a person last verified the entry against real CVE and
  NVD data.

## How an entry is checked

A wrong name in the catalog would silently mean "no vulnerabilities". Three
things guard against that:

1. A person checks every entry against a real CVE record and NVD entry before it
   is added, and sets `checked:` to that date. The evidence (the NVD hit counts,
   the CNA names from real records, the KEV names and the endoflife slug) is kept in
   `catalog/VERIFIED.md`.
2. `cargo xtask catalog verify` re-checks the CPE, KEV and endoflife keys against
   the live sources. It runs weekly in the repository. It cannot check CNA keys,
   because CVE.org cannot be searched by vendor.
3. When the daily database is built, a product whose names match nothing in the
   data is marked unverified. A stack item with such a product shows up as an
   `unknown` finding with the rule `UNP-UNVERIFIED-PRODUCT`, so an empty result
   is never read as "safe".

Known gaps are listed at the top of `catalog/VERIFIED.md`. For example, a few
products have no CNA keys because every record names them `n/a`; matching uses
the CPE (and KEV) keys for them.

## Ask for a product

If something you run is not here, it cannot be matched yet. Open an issue with
the **Add a product** template at
<https://github.com/Amet13/unpatched/issues/new/choose> and give:

- the product name and vendor, and where its releases are published
- how its versions look (`7.2.5`, `2024.10.1`, `15.4`) and whether they follow
  semver, calendar versioning or something unusual
- one CVE that affects it, so the names can be checked against a real record
- its endoflife.date page, if there is one

Or add it yourself: copy a similar file in `catalog/`, fix the names, add a corpus
case for one affected and one fixed version, and run `cargo xtask check`. The steps
are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Amet13/unpatched/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#adding-a-product).
A person checks every new entry before it is merged.

For a library or an operating system package that is not a catalog product, use a
`purl` in your stack instead: those are looked up in OSV and need no catalog entry.
See the [config reference](config.md#the-stack).

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/action.html

# GitHub Action


`amet13/unpatched` is a composite Action. It downloads the release binary for the
runner, checks its SHA-256 against the release, caches it, runs
`unpatched check --notify`, and writes the report to the run summary. The
step-by-step setup is on [Start with GitHub](start-github.md).

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v7
- uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
```

It needs `actions/checkout` before it (to read `unpatched.yml`) and the job
permissions `contents: read` and `issues: write`. It sets `GITHUB_TOKEN` for
itself. Linux, macOS and Windows runners are supported, on x86_64 and, except for
Windows, arm64.

## Inputs


| Input | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `args` | empty | Extra arguments for `unpatched check`, for example `--exit-code --verbose`. |
| `binary` | empty | Path to an unpatched binary you built. Skips the download. Used by this repository's CI. |
| `config` | `unpatched.yml` | Path to your stack file. |
| `db` | empty | Path to a database file. Empty: download the daily database. |
| `dry-run` | `false` | Send nothing and write no issues; only print what would happen. |
| `version` | empty | The unpatched release to run, like v3.0.0, v3.1.0-rc.1 or v3 (the newest stable v3.x.y). Empty: the version in the tag you used (`uses: amet13/unpatched@v3.0.0`), else the latest release. Set it when you pin the action to a commit SHA (`uses: amet13/unpatched@<sha>`), because a SHA says nothing about the version. |


`version` takes a full tag (`v3.0.0`), or a major or minor prefix (`v3`, `v3.0`),
which means the newest published release that starts with it. It defaults to the
version in the tag you wrote after `@`, and to the latest release when that is a
branch or a commit. The checksum comes from the `.sha256` file of the same
release; on a mismatch the Action stops and does not run the file.

The action always passes `--notify --format markdown` and writes the report to the
run summary (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`). `args` adds options to `unpatched check`, split on
spaces.

## Outputs

The Action has no outputs. The report is in the run summary, findings are in
issues, and the exit code of the step is the exit code of `unpatched`: see
[Exit codes](start-cli.md#exit-codes). With `args: --exit-code` the step fails
(exit code 1) when something is to be fixed today, which turns the run red in the
Actions tab and sends GitHub's own failure email.

## Secrets for chat channels

The Action reads secrets from the environment of the step. Set the ones you use:

```yaml
- uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
  env:
    UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN }}
    UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK: ${{ secrets.UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
```

Names for each channel are on [Notifications](notifications.md).

## Examples

**Pin an exact release**, so an upgrade is your decision:

```yaml
- uses: amet13/unpatched@v3.0.0
```

**Try it without side effects.** Prints what would happen; opens no issues and
sends nothing:

```yaml
- uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
  with:
    dry-run: "true"
```

**Fail the run on a "fix today" finding**, and see more in the summary:

```yaml
- uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
  with:
    args: --exit-code --verbose
```

**Another config path**, if the file is not called `unpatched.yml` or is in a folder:

```yaml
- uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
  with:
    config: infra/stack.yml
```

Use one config per repository. Issues, the status issue and the delivery state
belong to the repository, and a run closes every issue whose finding is not in
*its* report. Two configs in one repository would close each other's issues. An
MSP uses one private repository per client.

**A database you built or downloaded yourself:**

```yaml
- uses: amet13/unpatched@v3
  with:
    db: ./unpatched-db.sqlite
```

**A binary you built** (used by this repository's own tests): `binary: target/release/unpatched`
skips the download.

## Behaviour to know

- A run does not commit and does not need `contents: write`.
- A scheduled workflow is paused by GitHub after 60 days without repository
  activity **in public repositories**. Private repositories are not paused.
- The cache key is the release tag and the runner, so the binary is downloaded
  once per release and runner.

---

Source: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/cli.html

# Command reference


`unpatched <command> [options]`. The help below is the program's own, written by
`cargo xtask docs`. Run `unpatched <command> --help` for the same on your machine.

## Global options

These work with every command, before or after its name:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--config FILE` | Your stack and settings. Default `unpatched.yml`. |
| `--db FILE` | The vulnerability database. Default `$UNPATCHED_DB`, else the cache folder. |
| `--offline` | No network: no database download and no OSV lookups for packages. |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | More detail: evidence in reports; `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs. |
| `--quiet` | Print only what was asked for, and errors. Cannot be used with `-v`. |
| `--color WHEN` | `auto` (default), `always` or `never`. |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | OK |
| 1 | `check --exit-code` found something to fix today |
| 2 | Usage or configuration error: bad YAML, unknown product, a missing secret |
| 3 | Data error: no database, database too old, a download or source failed |
| 4 | Delivery error: a notification channel or GitHub issue failed |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `UNPATCHED_DB` | The same as `--db`. |
| `UNPATCHED_DB_URL` | Where `check` and `db update` download the database from. Default: the `db` release of `Amet13/unpatched`. |
| `UNPATCHED_CACHE_DIR` | Where the downloaded database is kept. Default: your system's cache folder, plus `unpatched`. |
| `UNPATCHED_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, `UNPATCHED_SLACK_WEBHOOK`, `UNPATCHED_DISCORD_WEBHOOK`, `UNPATCHED_NTFY_TOKEN`, `UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_URL`, `UNPATCHED_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Secrets for [notifications](notifications.md). |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_API_URL` | Used for GitHub issues (set by GitHub Actions). |

## Commands


### `unpatched`

```text
Tells you when software you run has a vulnerability you need to act on

Usage: unpatched [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  check    Match your stack against the database and print the report
  init     Write a starting unpatched.yml (and, with --github, the workflow)
  explain  Show the evidence: a rule id, a CVE, or a finding key
  search   Find a product in the catalog
  catalog  The products unpatched knows
  db       The vulnerability database
  mcp      Run the MCP server on stdio, for AI agents
  schema   Print a JSON Schema
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --config <FILE>  Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
      --db <FILE>      The vulnerability database (default: $UNPATCHED_DB, else the cache directory) [env: UNPATCHED_DB=]
      --offline        Use no network: no database download and no package (OSV) lookups
  -v, --verbose...     More detail (evidence in reports, `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs)
      --quiet          Print only what was asked for, and errors
      --color <WHEN>   When to use colour [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version

Exit codes:
  0  ok
  1  `check --exit-code` found something to fix today
  2  usage or configuration error
  3  data error (no database, database too old, a download or source failed)
  4  delivery error (a notification channel or GitHub issue failed)

Docs: https://amet13.github.io/unpatched/
```

### `unpatched check`

```text
Match your stack against the database and print the report

Usage: unpatched check [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <FILE>    Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
      --format <FORMAT>  How to print the report [default: text] [possible values: text, json, markdown, sarif]
      --db <FILE>        The vulnerability database (default: $UNPATCHED_DB, else the cache directory) [env: UNPATCHED_DB=]
      --output <FILE>    Write the report to FILE instead of stdout. A file named by $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is appended to, so other steps keep their text
      --exit-code        Exit with 1 when something has to be fixed today
      --offline          Use no network: no database download and no package (OSV) lookups
      --notify           Also send the findings to the configured channels (issues, chat)
  -v, --verbose...       More detail (evidence in reports, `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs)
      --dry-run          With --notify: send and write nothing; print what would happen
      --quiet            Print only what was asked for, and errors
      --color <WHEN>     When to use colour [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
      --github           Keep delivery state and issues in GitHub (automatic inside GitHub Actions)
      --allow-stale      Do not fail when the database is older than `stale_fail_days`
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

### `unpatched init`

```text
Write a starting unpatched.yml (and, with --github, the workflow)

Usage: unpatched init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <FILE>  Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
      --github         Also write .github/workflows/unpatched.yml
      --db <FILE>      The vulnerability database (default: $UNPATCHED_DB, else the cache directory) [env: UNPATCHED_DB=]
      --force          Overwrite files that exist
      --offline        Use no network: no database download and no package (OSV) lookups
  -v, --verbose...     More detail (evidence in reports, `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs)
      --quiet          Print only what was asked for, and errors
      --color <WHEN>   When to use colour [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

### `unpatched explain`

```text
Show the evidence: a rule id, a CVE, or a finding key

Arguments:
  <TARGET>  `UNP-KEV`, `CVE-2024-21762` or a finding key such as `office-firewall/CVE-2024-21762`

Options:
      --config <FILE>  Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
      --db <FILE>      The vulnerability database (default: $UNPATCHED_DB, else the cache directory) [env: UNPATCHED_DB=]
      --offline        Use no network: no database download and no package (OSV) lookups
  -v, --verbose...     More detail (evidence in reports, `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs)
      --quiet          Print only what was asked for, and errors
      --color <WHEN>   When to use colour [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```


### `unpatched catalog list`

```text
List the products

Usage: unpatched catalog list [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <FILE>  Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
      --kind <KIND>    Only this kind of product [possible values: appliance, app, os, database, server, library, desktop, cms]
      --db <FILE>      The vulnerability database (default: $UNPATCHED_DB, else the cache directory) [env: UNPATCHED_DB=]
      --offline        Use no network: no database download and no package (OSV) lookups
  -v, --verbose...     More detail (evidence in reports, `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs)
      --quiet          Print only what was asked for, and errors
      --color <WHEN>   When to use colour [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

### `unpatched db info`

```text
Show what is in the database and how old it is

Usage: unpatched db info [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <FILE>  Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
      --json           Print the counts and the sources as JSON
      --db <FILE>      The vulnerability database (default: $UNPATCHED_DB, else the cache directory) [env: UNPATCHED_DB=]
      --offline        Use no network: no database download and no package (OSV) lookups
  -v, --verbose...     More detail (evidence in reports, `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs)
      --quiet          Print only what was asked for, and errors
      --color <WHEN>   When to use colour [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
```

### `unpatched db build`

```text
Build the database from the sources (slow; CI does this daily)

Usage: unpatched db build [OPTIONS] --out <FILE>

Options:
      --config <FILE>     Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
      --out <FILE>        Where to write. A name ending in `.zst` is compressed
      --cvelist <DIR>     A checkout of CVEProject/cvelistV5. Without it CVE.org is skipped
      --db <FILE>         The vulnerability database (default: $UNPATCHED_DB, else the cache directory) [env: UNPATCHED_DB=]
      --nvd-years <A..B>  NVD years to read, like `2018..2026` (default: all)
      --offline           Use no network: no database download and no package (OSV) lookups
      --nvd-cache <DIR>   Keep downloaded NVD feeds here between builds
  -v, --verbose...        More detail (evidence in reports, `-v` info logs, `-vv` debug logs)
      --quiet             Print only what was asked for, and errors
      --strict            Fail, and write nothing, when any source failed (CI uses this)
      --color <WHEN>      When to use colour [default: auto] [possible values: auto, always, never]
  -h, --help              Print help
  -V, --version           Print version
```

### `unpatched db sources-health`

```text
Ask every source for one known item; fails when any source fails

Options:
      --config <FILE>  Your stack and settings [default: unpatched.yml]
```
